question: What is the ascension of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to the heavens called?
why: Mi'raj means the ascension from Masjid al-Aqsa up through the heavens. Isra is only the night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem. Ghazwah is a battle and Umrah is the lesser pilgrimage.
rel: Isra and Mi'raj happened about one year before Hijrah. Surah Bani Israil (Al-Isra) starts with the Isra.

question: Which fundamental act of worship was prescribed during the event of Mi'raj?
why: The five daily prayers (Salah) were made obligatory on the night of Mi'raj. Fasting and Zakat came in 2 AH in Madinah, and Hajj was made obligatory later (about 9 AH).
rel: At first 50 prayers were ordered, then reduced to 5 with the reward of 50. Salah is the only worship made obligatory in the heavens.

question: From which sacred mosque did the night journey begin in Makkah?
why: The Isra began at Masjid al-Haram in Makkah, as Surah Al-Isra verse 1 says. Masjid al-Aqsa was the end point of the journey. Quba and Masjid an-Nabawi are in Madinah and were built after Hijrah.
rel: Isra: Masjid al-Haram to Masjid al-Aqsa on the Buraq. Masjid al-Aqsa was the first Qiblah.

question: What were the pledges made between Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and people from Yathrib called?
why: The people of Yathrib gave their pledges at Aqabah near Mina, so they are called the Pledges of Aqabah. Hudaybiyyah (6 AH) was a treaty with Quraysh, the Charter of Madinah came after Hijrah, and Ridwan was under a tree at Hudaybiyyah.
rel: First Aqabah: 12 men (621 CE). Second Aqabah: about 73 men and 2 women (622 CE).

question: What was the earlier name of Madinah?
why: Madinah was called Yathrib before Hijrah; it became Madinat-un-Nabi, the City of the Prophet. Bakkah is an old name of Makkah, Faran is a name linked to the Makkah area, and Khaybar is a separate oasis north of Madinah.
rel: Madinah is also called Taybah. Makkah is also called Umm al-Qura.

question: Who was sent to Yathrib as an early Muslim teacher after the First Pledge of Aqabah?
why: Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA) was the first teacher (envoy) of Islam sent to Yathrib. Abu Bakr and Bilal stayed in Makkah, and Mu'adh ibn Jabal was a man of Madinah, later sent to Yemen.
rel: Mus'ab ibn Umayr was the standard-bearer martyred at Uhud. Mu'adh ibn Jabal was sent to Yemen as governor and teacher.

question: Who slept in Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) bed on the night of Hijrah?
why: Ali (RA) slept in the Prophet's bed to trick the Quraysh and later returned people's trusts (amanat). Abu Bakr travelled with the Prophet, Umar had migrated openly earlier, and Uthman had gone to Abyssinia and Madinah.
rel: Hijrah took place in 622 CE (Rabi al-Awwal, 1 AH era). Ali joined the Prophet in Quba a few days later.

question: Who accompanied Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) during the migration to Madinah?
why: Abu Bakr (RA) was the Prophet's companion on the Hijrah and in the cave (Surah At-Tawbah 9:40). Ali stayed back in Makkah, Umar migrated before, and Zayd went with the Prophet to Taif, not on Hijrah.
rel: Abdullah ibn Urayqit was their guide. Asma bint Abi Bakr brought food and got the title Dhat an-Nitaqayn.

question: In which cave did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and Abu Bakr (RA) take refuge during Hijrah?
why: They hid for three nights in the Cave of Thawr, south of Makkah. Cave Hira is where the first revelation came, and Uhud and Quba are places in Madinah.
rel: Cave Hira is on Jabal an-Nur. The spider web and the dove's nest at Thawr are famous stories.

question: Who was the leader of the hypocrites in Madinah commonly mentioned in Seerah?
why: Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul led the hypocrites (Munafiqun) in Madinah. Abu Jahl was an open enemy in Makkah, Musaylimah was a false prophet, and Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf was a Jewish poet.
rel: Ibn Ubayy went back with about 300 men before Uhud. Surah Al-Munafiqun is about the hypocrites.

question: Which Jewish scholar of Madinah accepted Islam and became a companion?
why: Abdullah ibn Salam (RA), a rabbi of Banu Qaynuqa, accepted Islam soon after Hijrah. Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and Huyayy ibn Akhtab stayed enemies, and Abu Jahl was a pagan of Makkah.
rel: Huyayy ibn Akhtab was a chief of Banu Nadir. Safiyyah (RA), his daughter, became a wife of the Prophet.

question: What title was given to the Muslims of Madinah who welcomed the emigrants?
why: Ansar means helpers; they were the Muslims of Madinah (Aws and Khazraj). Muhajirun were the emigrants from Makkah, Tabi'un came after the companions, and Ashab al-Suffah lived on the Suffah platform.
rel: The Ansar came from two tribes: Aws and Khazraj. The Prophet made brotherhood (Mu'akhat) between Ansar and Muhajirun.

question: What was the platform in Masjid an-Nabawi associated with companions devoted to learning?
why: The Suffah was a shaded platform where poor companions lived and learned; it is called the first residential school of Islam. The Mihrab is the prayer niche, the Minbar is the pulpit, and the Rawdah is the area between the pulpit and the Prophet's house.
rel: Abu Hurairah (RA) was one of the famous Ashab al-Suffah. Masjid an-Nabawi was built in 1 AH.

question: Which companion reported a dream containing the wording of the Adhan?
why: Abdullah ibn Zayd (RA) saw the words of the Adhan in a dream and told the Prophet, who approved them. Bilal was told to call it because of his strong voice. Uthman and Abu Bakr did not report this dream.
rel: The Adhan began in 1 AH (some say 2 AH) in Madinah. Bilal (RA) was the first Mu'adhdhin.
note: PDF option A was Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA); changed to Uthman because Umar also saw the same dream, so two answers could be right.

question: Who became the most famous early Mu'adhdhin of Islam?
why: Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) was the first and most famous Mu'adhdhin of the Prophet. Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum was a second Mu'adhdhin but less famous, while Ammar and Salman were not Mu'adhdhins.
rel: Bilal gave the Adhan on the Kaaba at the Conquest of Makkah (8 AH). His former master was Umayyah ibn Khalaf.

question: In which month of 2 AH was fasting in Ramadan made obligatory?
why: The order to fast in Ramadan came in Sha'ban of 2 AH, just before the first Ramadan in Madinah. Ramadan is the month of fasting itself, not the month the order came, and Rajab and Shawwal are wrong months.
rel: The Qiblah was also changed in 2 AH (Rajab or Sha'ban). Battle of Badr was on 17 Ramadan 2 AH.

question: In which year of Hijrah was the obligation of Ramadan fasting introduced?
why: Fasting in Ramadan became obligatory in 2 AH. In 1 AH Masjid an-Nabawi was built, 5 AH was the Battle of the Trench, and 9 AH is when Hajj became obligatory (per most scholars).
rel: Zakat and Eid prayers also started in 2 AH. Surah Al-Baqarah 2:183 is the fasting verse.

question: In which direction did Muslims pray before the Qiblah was changed to the Kaaba?
why: Muslims first prayed toward Bait al-Maqdis (Masjid al-Aqsa) in Jerusalem for about 16-17 months after Hijrah. Damascus, Cairo and Mount Sinai were never the Qiblah.
rel: The Qiblah changed to the Kaaba in 2 AH (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:144). Masjid al-Aqsa is called the first Qiblah.

question: Which mosque is associated with the change of Qiblah during prayer?
why: Masjid al-Qiblatayn means the mosque of two Qiblahs, because the Qiblah changed during a prayer there. Quba is the first mosque built in Islam, Masjid an-Nabawi is the Prophet's mosque, and al-Ghamamah is linked to Eid prayer.
rel: Masjid Quba is the first mosque of Islam. The Qiblah change came in 2 AH.

question: Which daughter of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) married Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA)?
why: Fatimah (RA) married Ali (RA) in 2 AH. Zaynab married Abu al-As, and Ruqayyah and then Umm Kulthum married Uthman (RA).
rel: Uthman (RA) is called Dhun-Nurayn because he married two daughters of the Prophet. Hasan and Husayn were sons of Ali and Fatimah.

question: Which expedition is regarded as the first Ghazwah led personally by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
why: Ghazwah al-Abwa (Waddan), in Safar 2 AH, was the first expedition the Prophet led himself. Buwat, Safwan (first Badr) and Ushayrah came after it in the same year.
rel: Ushayrah led to a treaty with Banu Mudlij. Badr al-Kubra (17 Ramadan 2 AH) was the first big battle.

question: What is a military campaign attended personally by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) called?
why: A Ghazwah is a campaign in which the Prophet himself took part. A Sariyyah is one he sent without going himself, Hijrah is migration, and Umrah is the lesser pilgrimage.
rel: Most counts give 27 Ghazwat and about 50 or more Saraya. The last Ghazwah was Tabuk (9 AH).

question: Which prominent Quraysh leader was killed at Badr?
why: Abu Jahl (Amr ibn Hisham) was killed at Badr by the young Mu'adh and Mu'awwidh, and finished by Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. Abu Sufyan, Ikrimah and Amr ibn al-Aas survived and later accepted Islam.
rel: Abu Jahl was called the Pharaoh of this Ummah. Abu Sufyan led the Quraysh caravan before Badr.

question: How many Muslims were martyred at the Battle of Badr according to accounts?
why: 14 Muslims were martyred at Badr (6 Muhajirun and 8 Ansar). 70 is the number of Quraysh killed at Badr and also of Muslims martyred at Uhud, so it is wrong here.
rel: 313 Muslims fought about 1,000 Quraysh at Badr. 70 Quraysh were killed and 70 captured.

question: Approximately how many Quraysh fighters were killed at Badr?
why: About 70 Quraysh were killed and about 70 were taken prisoner at Badr. 14 is the number of Muslim martyrs, and 100 and 300 are not given in the accounts.
rel: Badr was on 17 Ramadan 2 AH (624 CE). The Muslims were 313 against about 1,000.

question: Which daughter of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) died around the time of the Battle of Badr?
why: Ruqayyah (RA), wife of Uthman, died in Madinah while the Muslims were at Badr; Uthman stayed back to nurse her. Zaynab died in 8 AH, Umm Kulthum in 9 AH, and Fatimah after the Prophet.
rel: Uthman then married Umm Kulthum and got the title Dhun-Nurayn. Uthman got a share of Badr booty though absent.

question: What educational condition was set for releasing certain literate prisoners after Badr?
options: Teach children to read and write
why: Literate prisoners who could not pay ransom were freed after each taught 10 Muslim children to read and write. Ransom was for those who could pay, no one was forced to convert, and building houses was not a condition.
rel: Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) learned writing this way. Ransom per prisoner was about 1,000 to 4,000 dirhams.

question: What name does the Qur'an use for the day of the Battle of Badr?
why: Surah Al-Anfal 8:41 calls Badr Yaum al-Furqan, the Day of Criterion between truth and falsehood. Fath refers to the Conquest of Makkah, Ahzab to the Trench, and Jumu'ah is Friday.
rel: Surah Al-Anfal was revealed about Badr. Surah Al-Ahzab is about the Battle of the Trench (5 AH).

question: According to the Qur'an, how many angels were initially promised as reinforcement at Badr?
why: Surah Al-Anfal 8:9 says Allah helped with a thousand angels one after another. 3,000 and 5,000 are mentioned in Surah Al-Imran as further promises, and 100 and 10,000 are not mentioned.
rel: Surah Al-Imran 3:124-125 mentions 3,000 and 5,000 angels. 10,000 was the size of the Muslim army at the Conquest of Makkah.

question: Who was the former master of Bilal (RA) who was killed at Badr?
why: Umayyah ibn Khalaf tortured Bilal (RA) in Makkah and was killed at Badr. Utbah and Walid were killed in the first duels at Badr but were not Bilal's masters, and Abu Lahab did not go to Badr and died in Makkah.
rel: Abu Bakr (RA) bought and freed Bilal. Hamza, Ali and Ubaydah fought the first duels at Badr.

question: Which uncle of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was captured at Badr?
why: Abbas (RA) fought on the Quraysh side and was taken prisoner, then paid ransom. Abu Talib had died before Hijrah, Hamza fought for the Muslims, and Abu Lahab did not join the battle.
rel: Abbas openly accepted Islam before the Conquest of Makkah. Abu Lahab died a few days after Badr.

question: Which Jewish tribe was expelled from Madinah after the conflict following Badr?
why: Banu Qaynuqa broke the treaty after Badr and were expelled in 2 AH. Banu Nadir were expelled in 4 AH, Banu Qurayzah were punished after the Trench in 5 AH, and Ghatafan was an Arab tribe, not Jewish.
rel: The three Jewish tribes of Madinah: Qaynuqa, Nadir, Qurayzah. Surah Al-Hashr is about Banu Nadir.

question: Which cousin of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) distinguished himself in the fighting at Badr?
why: Ali (RA), the Prophet's cousin, won his duel against Walid ibn Utbah and fought bravely at Badr. Abu Bakr was not a cousin and stayed with the Prophet at the command shelter, Uthman was absent, and Mu'adh ibn Jabal was not a cousin.
rel: Ali got the sword Dhul-Fiqar at Badr. Hamza (RA) killed Utbah ibn Rabi'ah in the duels.

question: Which Surah contains the final explicit Qur'anic prohibition of intoxicants?
why: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:90-91 gave the final, complete ban on wine and gambling. Al-Baqarah 2:219 only said the harm is greater than the benefit, while Al-Fil and Al-Kawthar are short Makki surahs not about intoxicants.
rel: Wine was banned in stages: Al-Baqarah 2:219, An-Nisa 4:43, then Al-Ma'idah 5:90. The final ban came around 3-4 AH.

question: Which expedition is commonly known as the Battle of Sawiq?
why: Ghazwah as-Sawiq (2 AH) was the chase of Abu Sufyan after his raid near Madinah; his men threw away bags of sawiq (barley flour) while fleeing. Uhud, Khandaq and Khaybar were different, bigger battles.
rel: Sawiq means barley flour. Abu Sufyan made this raid to fulfil his oath after Badr.

question: In which Islamic month and year did the Battle of Uhud take place?
why: Uhud was fought in Shawwal 3 AH (March 625 CE). Ramadan 2 AH was Badr, and the other dates do not match any of these battles.
rel: Battle of the Trench: Shawwal/Dhul Qa'dah 5 AH. Badr: 17 Ramadan 2 AH.

question: How many Muslims initially set out toward Uhud before a group withdrew?
why: About 1,000 Muslims set out; Abdullah ibn Ubayy then left with about 300, leaving about 700. 313 was Badr, 3,000 was the Quraysh army, and 700 is the number left after the withdrawal.
rel: About 700 Muslims fought at Uhud against 3,000 Quraysh. 313 Muslims fought at Badr.

question: Approximately how many Quraysh soldiers participated in the Battle of Uhud?
why: The Quraysh came to Uhud with about 3,000 soldiers under Abu Sufyan. 1,000 was their number at Badr, and 10,000 was the size of the allied army at the Trench (Ahzab).
rel: The Quraysh had about 200 horses at Uhud. At the Trench the confederates had about 10,000.

question: How many archers were positioned to guard the Muslim army's rear at Uhud?
why: The Prophet placed 50 archers on the hill of Ainain (Jabal ar-Rumat) to guard the rear. About 10 stayed back when the others left, and 100 and 200 are wrong.
rel: The archers' hill is called Jabal ar-Rumat (Hill of Archers). Their leader was Abdullah ibn Jubayr.

question: Who commanded the archers positioned at Uhud?
why: Abdullah ibn Jubayr (RA) led the 50 archers and stayed at his post until he was martyred. Mus'ab held the standard, Hamza fought in the main army, and Khalid was then on the Quraysh side.
rel: Mus'ab ibn Umayr was the standard-bearer at Uhud. Khalid ibn al-Walid accepted Islam in 8 AH.

question: Which military commander exploited the opening left by archers at Uhud?
why: Khalid ibn al-Walid led the Quraysh cavalry around the hill and attacked from behind when the archers left. Abu Sufyan was the overall leader, and Ikrimah helped Khalid but did not lead the attack; Amr ibn al-Aas did not lead it.
rel: Khalid later got the title Saifullah (Sword of Allah) at Mu'tah. He accepted Islam in 8 AH.

question: Which uncle of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), the Lion of Allah, was martyred at Uhud?
why: Hamza (RA), Asadullah, was martyred at Uhud by Wahshi's spear. Abu Talib died before Hijrah, Abbas lived long after, and Ja'far was a cousin martyred at Mu'tah.
rel: Hamza is called Sayyid ash-Shuhada (leader of the martyrs). Ja'far is called Ja'far at-Tayyar.

question: Who was the Muslim standard-bearer martyred at Uhud?
why: Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA) carried the flag at Uhud and was martyred holding it. Ali took the flag after him and survived, Hamza was martyred but not as flag-bearer, and Sa'd was an archer who survived.
rel: Mus'ab was the first teacher sent to Yathrib. He looked like the Prophet, so some thought the Prophet was killed.

question: How many Muslims were martyred at the Battle of Uhud according to accounts?
why: About 70 Muslims were martyred at Uhud, most of them Ansar. 14 was Badr's number of martyrs, 313 was the Muslim army at Badr, and 100 is not given.
rel: Quraysh lost about 22-23 men at Uhud. Martyrs of Uhud are buried near Jabal Uhud.

question: What injury did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) sustain during the Battle of Uhud?
why: At Uhud a front tooth (lower right) of the Prophet was broken and two rings of his helmet went into his cheek. He did not break his arm, did not lose his sight, and was not unhurt.
rel: Abu Ubaydah (RA) pulled out the helmet rings with his teeth. Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas threw the stone that hurt the Prophet.

question: Which companion is remembered for defending Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) at Uhud?
why: Talhah (RA) shielded the Prophet with his own body and his hand was paralysed by arrows. Abu Lahab was an enemy who died after Badr, Ibn Ubayy left before the battle, and Musaylimah was a false prophet.
rel: Talhah is one of the Ashara Mubashara (ten promised Paradise). Abu Dujanah and Nusaybah bint Ka'b also shielded the Prophet at Uhud.

question: What major lesson is drawn from Uhud regarding the Muslim archers?
options: Obedience to the Prophet (PBUH) was essential
why: The archers left their post against the Prophet's clear order, and the Muslims lost the upper hand; so the lesson is obedience. Leaving early caused the loss, cavalry was in fact used against them, and returning to Makkah makes no sense.
rel: Surah Al-Imran (verses 121-175) discusses Uhud. The archers were told not to leave even if birds snatched the army.
